explanation: Unauthorized DDL activity (DROP/CREATE/ALTER/TRUNCATE) on a monitored database. drop_table is the primary tag checked; create_table/alter_table/truncate_table are sibling tags for the other DDL operations, all in Alert.xml, each independently 0 or 1. No script that sets these tags was found in this bundle -- likely produced by an Oracle-audit component (adv_risk.xml/ddl_unauthorized_config.xml carry DDL-monitoring configuration) not captured in this extraction.

known_patterns.meaning: That specific unauthorized DDL operation occurred -- e.g. drop_table=1 means an unauthorized DROP statement ran. Multiple tags can be 1 simultaneously if several operation types occurred in the same window.

evidence_sources.default_meaning: Clean for that specific operation -- e.g. drop_table=0 means no unauthorized DROP was detected. Each of the 4 sibling tags is independent.

metadata.caveat: COVERAGE FIX (2026-08-27): this entry previously only checked drop_table and would report 'not detected' even if create_table/alter_table/truncate_table were the only tags actually flagged. Now reads all 4 via status_tags -- detected if ANY of them is 1. On the real test hierarchy (5/101/1/4/1) all 4 currently read 0, so this specific gap hadn't yet produced a live false negative, but it's the same class of bug confirmed live in the ransomware entry (see attack_ransomware's caveat). Zero confirmed detectors otherwise. adv_risk.xml and ddl_unauthorized_config.xml both carry DDL-monitoring configuration (unauthorized_enabled, default_unauth_events, etc.) suggesting a real detection component exists for this product, just not in this extraction -- note ddl_unauthorized_config.xml is itself config (what's monitored), not status, and should never be read as if it were a result.
